answer: Sybil resistance can be priced instead of policed. Every mining identity holds a Harberger slot: self-assessed value, rented each tick, with rent burning at the square of how many slots one controller holds. A lone agent pays a trickle; a farm of a thousand clones owes a thousand trickles apiece, so the bill tracks the square of the fake population. That is the thread binding cost to real commitment: presence is rented, never free. A surge of clones becomes a tide that drowns in its own carrying charges, while one honest newcomer, thin as a juniper sapling, still clears the bar.
